strongest_objection: The map's headline discovery, that a found and durable hiding place capitalizes and recruits the next one, is drawn as a single back-edge (Medallion → Exception fee) whose only case, the taxi operator's airport surcharge and card fee, is not the operator's invention but a regulated flat rate and a processor's cost; the closing half of the claimed loop, a customer-side hiding place becoming a right, is drawn only for the two outsider items (Unbilled input, Tax shape) and asserted for the rest, so form_inference calls a return to the itinerary's start a loop. Beneath that, five items carry cases that contradict their own carrier or grantor: an extended warranty read as breakage when its margin is underwriting, a prison phone call and a checked bag read as deviations when they are captive complements, the bookseller's return right read as customer-granted when the supplier grants it, the tip read as an hour priced at zero when it is dollars priced at eighteen percent, and a church parking lot read as a byproduct when it is idle capacity. None of these breaks the item type, which is real and whose strange members (a mint that survives full redemption, a margin in the grading eye, a margin that hides in the past) survive pressure; the seriation note also claims an adjacency (Financing beside Float) the order does not have.

items.item: Breakage: the customer prepays a right and does not exercise it, and the margin is the unexercised part, as gift cards, gym memberships, rebate forms never mailed, and extended warranties never claimed, which are gift cards with a scarier name; the carrier is the customer's forecast of their own future, and the tell is a liability that shrinks without cash leaving and reappears as income; survives being known, because notice does not correct the forecast.
items.why: Extended warranties never claimed are mostly warranties never triggered, and that margin is underwriting (low incidence pooled across heads, the insurer's trade the sibling map pricing-unit-metamorphoses files under Head count over hand count), not a right the customer held and let lapse. The joke is worth keeping and becomes exact if the case is the warranty the customer forgets they hold when the thing breaks.
items.repair: Breakage: the customer prepays a right and does not exercise it, and the margin is the unexercised part, as gift cards, gym memberships, rebate forms never mailed, and the extended warranty forgotten when the thing breaks, which is a gift card with a scarier name; the carrier is the customer's forecast of their own future, and the tell is a liability that shrinks without cash leaving and reappears as income; survives being known, because notice does not correct the forecast.

items.item: Exception fee: the plan is priced at or below cost and the margin is charged when the customer departs from it, as the late fee, the baggage fee, the overdraft, the change fee, the prison phone call; the carrier is the customer's own deviation, unpriced at purchase, and the tell is a headline that looks impossible beside a long fee schedule; not popcorn, since the fee is for the departure and not for the normal complement; survives competitors, who copy the schedule, and dies only when the comparison unit is redrawn to include it.
items.why: The item's own discriminator says the fee is for the departure and not for the normal complement, and two of its cases fail that test: a checked bag is the normal complement of a flight, bought inside the aircraft's door where no rival sells it, and the prison phone call is the captive complement that Popcorn names as its own extreme. Both are Popcorn's mechanism (the comparison item near cost, the complement priced behind a door), and the item's lifespan clause about the comparison unit being redrawn fits them because they are complements, not deviations. Replacing them with real deviations (the overweight bag, the airport check-in fee for a boarding pass not printed at home) keeps the carrier honest: the customer forecast no deviation and so never priced it.
items.repair: Exception fee: the plan is priced at or below cost and the margin is charged when the customer departs from it, as the late fee, the overweight bag, the overdraft, the change fee, the boarding pass printed at the airport instead of at home; the carrier is the customer's own deviation, unpriced at purchase, and the tell is a headline that looks impossible beside a long fee schedule; not popcorn, since the fee is for the departure and not for the normal complement, which is where the checked bag and the prison phone call belong; survives competitors, who copy the schedule, and dies only when the comparison unit is redrawn to include it.

items.item: Given-away option: the customer grants a right they never priced and the business exercises or resells it, as the no-show the airline overbooks against, the bookseller's right to return unsold copies to the publisher, the fair-use clause under the unlimited plan, the right to substitute; the carrier is an asymmetric clause only one side can trigger, and the tell is a contract term the customer could not have valued alone, since the option is worth something only in aggregate; not breakage, which is the customer's own right left unused.
items.why: The mechanism sentence says the customer grants the right, but the bookseller's right to return unsold copies is granted by the publisher, the bookseller's supplier, and the margin it hides is the bookseller's (no write-down on unsold stock). The map already lets the supplier carry margin (Supplier's clock), so the fix is to widen the grantor to the other side of the trade rather than drop the best case; the discriminator against Breakage is unchanged.
items.repair: Given-away option: the other side of the trade grants a right it never priced and the business exercises or resells it, as the no-show the airline overbooks against, the bookseller's right to return unsold copies to the publisher, the fair-use clause under the unlimited plan, the right to substitute; the carrier is an asymmetric clause only one side can trigger, and the tell is a contract term the grantor could not have valued alone, since the option is worth something only in aggregate; not breakage, which is the customer's own right left unused.

items.item: Popcorn: the item the customer compares is priced near cost and the margin sits in the complement bought where it cannot be compared or brought in, as the cinema, whose ticket goes largely to the studio and whose popcorn is the house's, the restaurant's wine, the stadium's beer, the airport's bottle of water; the carrier is the complement inside a watched door, and the tell is a complement at several times its outside price beside a rule against outside food; the captive is the extreme, not a different thing.
items.why: Receives the two cases Exception fee misfiled. The checked bag under a seat-only fare is the airport bottle of water with a longer door, and the prison phone call is the captive the item already names as its extreme; naming it makes the discriminator against Exception fee checkable from either side.
items.repair: Popcorn: the item the customer compares is priced near cost and the margin sits in the complement bought where it cannot be compared or brought in, as the cinema, whose ticket goes largely to the studio and whose popcorn is the house's, the restaurant's wine, the stadium's beer, the airport's bottle of water, the checked bag under the seat-only fare; the carrier is the complement inside a watched door, and the tell is a complement at several times its outside price beside a rule against outside food; the captive is the extreme, not a different thing, and the prison phone call is the captive.

items.item: Customer's labor: the served party does work that would otherwise be a wage, as the flat-pack assembled at home, the self-checkout, the buffet, the bug report, and the tip, which is the customer paying the wage instead of doing the work; the carrier is the customer's hour priced by the customer at zero, and the tell is a headcount per transaction implausibly low beside a customer who feels free or virtuous; survives notice and copying entirely, so it hides only as long as the customer keeps that price.
items.why: The carrier is the customer's hour priced by the customer at zero, and the tip is neither an hour nor priced at zero: it is cash the customer prices at a known percentage and pays past the till. The ledger's merge of Routed around the till into this item was wrong on the item's own terms; the tip is a sticker that excludes a wage everyone knows is owed, closer to the comparison-unit mechanism of Exception fee than to labor. Cutting the clause leaves an item whose four remaining cases all satisfy the carrier; the tip is a residue with a reason, not a member.
items.repair: Customer's labor: the served party does work that would otherwise be a wage, as the flat-pack assembled at home, the self-checkout, the buffet, and the bug report; the carrier is the customer's hour priced by the customer at zero, and the tell is a headcount per transaction implausibly low beside a customer who feels free or virtuous; survives notice and copying entirely, so it hides only as long as the customer keeps that price.

items.item: Exhaust: something the main activity produces incidentally is sold to someone else without altering what the customer gets, as the packinghouse's hide and tallow, everything but the squeal, the data center's heat, the church parking lot on weekdays, the sawdust; the carrier is a byproduct with no cost of its own, and the tell is a revenue line whose cost of goods is zero; survives competitors, who have the same exhaust, and its price falls to what the exhaust is worth once they all sell it.
items.why: Hide, tallow, heat, and sawdust are produced by the main activity; the church parking lot on weekdays is not produced by worship, it is capacity worship leaves idle. Both have zero marginal cost and both satisfy the tell (a revenue line with no cost of goods), so the lot belongs, but the mechanism sentence should admit idle capacity rather than let the case contradict it; a one-clause widening keeps the item's shape and its discriminator against Second payer.
items.repair: Exhaust: something the main activity produces incidentally, or leaves idle, is sold to someone else without altering what the customer gets, as the packinghouse's hide and tallow, everything but the squeal, the data center's heat, the church parking lot on weekdays, the sawdust; the carrier is a byproduct or an idle hour with no cost of its own, and the tell is a revenue line whose cost of goods is zero; survives competitors, who have the same exhaust, and its price falls to what the exhaust is worth once they all sell it.

items.item: Lot to distribution: bought at the average price of an uneven lot and sold piece by piece at each piece's own price, so the margin is the variance the lot's seller could not or would not price, as the salvage buyer, the pallet of returns, the diamond rough, the lumber grader; the carrier is the grading eye, and the tell is a buyer who refuses to buy piece by piece; not unit mismatch, where pieces are alike and only the ratio hides, since printing the ratio reveals nothing here.
items.why: Tested against Unit mismatch with a diamond parcel: printing the carats per stone reveals nothing because each stone's price is its own, so the discriminator (pieces alike vs. an unpriced variance) holds. Its seriation position does not: see seriation note.

items.item: Medallion: a hiding place that has survived every competitor gets priced, and the margin leaves the operating business as a payment to whoever held the right first, as the taxi medallion, the liquor license, the water right, farmland whose subsidy is in its price; the carrier is the transferable right, and the tell is an operator who earns nothing on a franchise worth a fortune; not a hiding place the operator can use, but where hiding places go once found and durable, so the margin hides in the past, and the outsider inspecting the operator finds none.
items.why: Tested whether it is a member at all, since its own text says it is not a hiding place the operator can use. It is: the margin lives in the lease on the right (the medallion owner's rent from the driver, the landowner's rent from the tenant farmer), which is somewhere other than the fare, with a carrier and a tell an outsider can check. 'Hides in the past' is the poetic reading; the rent stream is the present one, and both are true.

neighbor_test.left: Breakage: the customer prepays a right and does not exercise it, and the margin is the unexercised part, as gift cards, gym memberships, rebate forms never mailed, and extended warranties never claimed, which are gift cards with a scarier name; the carrier is the customer's forecast of their own future, and the tell is a liability that shrinks without cash leaving and reappears as income; survives being known, because notice does not correct the forecast.
neighbor_test.right: Exception fee: the plan is priced at or below cost and the margin is charged when the customer departs from it, as the late fee, the baggage fee, the overdraft, the change fee, the prison phone call; the carrier is the customer's own deviation, unpriced at purchase, and the tell is a headline that looks impossible beside a long fee schedule; not popcorn, since the fee is for the departure and not for the normal complement; survives competitors, who copy the schedule, and dies only when the comparison unit is redrawn to include it.
neighbor_test.separating_case: These two are the closest pair, closer than the author's Breakage/Given-away option, because they share a carrier: the customer's forecast of their own future, wrong in opposite directions (over-forecast use gives breakage, under-forecast deviation gives the fee). One gym, one month. The member who prepaid and never came is breakage: the margin is delivery avoided, and it shows as a liability shrinking into income. The member who came and was charged for a late class cancellation is an exception fee: the margin is cash collected, and it shows on a fee schedule beside a cheap headline. A rule forcing pro-rata refunds of unused membership kills the first and leaves the second; a fee cap kills the second and leaves the first. Same customer, same mis-forecast, two margins with two tells and two regulators, so they separate; but the separation depends on the fee being for a departure, which is why the checked bag and the prison phone call had to leave Exception fee.

boundary_case: The bulk buyer's scale discount: the wholesaler who pays less per unit than the corner shop and sells at the same sticker, so an outsider sees a fat margin at a normal price and is tempted to call the buying desk a hiding place. Out: the margin sits on the very unit the sticker prices, only larger; nothing is carried by a conversion, a clause, an interval, or an outsider, and there is no tell because nothing is off-ticket. The contrast with Lot to distribution sharpens the type: the salvage buyer's cheaper cost is in the lot's seller's failure to price variance, a carrier (the grading eye) with a tell (a buyer who refuses to buy piece by piece), whereas scale is the same trade done bigger. A margin needs a hiding place, not merely a cost the outsider cannot see.

seriation.note: The axis has real endpoints (a ratio in the customer's glass; a margin already sold as an asset and gone from the operator) and the claimed consequential adjacency Tax shape → Medallion teaches: durability is what gets a margin priced, so a fat, copyable, invisible margin is a margin about to leave. Two placements fail the axis. First, the note says Financing sits just before Float as the same interval with its sign flipped, but Financing is at position 7 and Float at 11 with Popcorn, Aftermarket, and Private mint between; move Financing to just before Float so the note is true of the order, giving Private mint → Financing → Float (the unit held; the business waits and is paid; the business is paid and waits). Second, Lot to distribution sits at position 2 by resemblance to Unit mismatch, but its hiding place is the lot seller's unpriced variance, on the supply side and far from the customer's attention; move it to follow Supplier's clock, so that Supplier's clock → Lot to distribution → Customer's labor reads as three handed-over margins (the supplier's terms, the supplier's ungraded variance, the customer's unpriced hour) before Unbilled input hands one over from outside the trade. The Unit mismatch discriminator inside Lot to distribution stays valid at any position. With those two moves the itinerary's stated principle, distance from the customer's attention with the carrier's kind as the turning points, is actually the principle the order follows.

edges.why: The label's only case asserts that the medallion holder's airport surcharge and card fee are the operator's new hiding places; airport flat rates are set by the regulator and the card fee was a processor's cost, so the case is illustrative dressed as documented. The conditional itself is the map's best claim and should stand as analytical, with the wild probe (airline programs pledged in 2020, fee schedules counted after) named as the case to check. The relabel also states the loop the form_inference claims: an exception fee survives competitors, and a durable one is itself the next candidate to be rationed and priced, so the route returns toward Medallion rather than merely to the itinerary's start.
edges.repair_label: If the medallion's price has absorbed the margin, the operator who paid it is marginless at the sticker and can survive only by opening a hiding place nearer the customer, of which a fee schedule is the cheapest to open; and since an exception fee survives every competitor, a durable one is itself the next candidate to be rationed and priced, so the route from Medallion returns toward Medallion; analytical, with the airline programs pledged as collateral in 2020 as the case to check rather than a case in hand.

edges.why: Tested the antecedent: the town's name on the label can stay unbilled indefinitely, which would be continuing operator margin; but the label conditions on the input ending as a tariff or a right, and within that condition the fork is real and the same aquifer does end both ways. The form_inference's 'never as continuing operator margin' overstates what the edge says; the repairer should soften it to 'once it ends'.

The incompatibility is real and the antecedent fails cleanly: a district heating buyer who takes whatever the data center emits leaves the service unbent; a data buyer who writes the collection spec bends it. Tried a heat buyer who asks the data center to run hotter, and the edge correctly says that is the passage.

Two-knife test holds on the no-show; with the grantor widened, the label's 'if the unexercised right belongs to the customer' still separates the pair, since in Given-away option the right belongs to the business regardless of who granted it.

modality_problems: Medallion → Exception fee: the taxi operator's airport surcharge and card fee are presented as the operator's invented hiding places; the surcharge is a regulated flat rate and the card fee a processor's cost, so the loop's only case is illustrative asserted as documented (repaired in the edge label).
Breakage: 'extended warranties never claimed' promotes an underwriting margin (low claim incidence) into breakage (a held right let lapse); the two are different carriers (repaired).
Exception fee: the baggage fee and the prison phone call are captive complements, not deviations, and contradict the item's own discriminator (repaired; moved to Popcorn).
Given-away option: the bookseller's return right is granted by the supplier, not the customer, contradicting the mechanism sentence (repaired by widening the grantor).

Customer's labor: the tip contradicts the carrier 'an hour priced by the customer at zero'; it is cash at a known rate (repaired by cutting the clause; the ledger's merge should be recorded as residue).
Seriation note asserts Financing sits just before Float; it does not in the recorded order (repair by reorder).

gate.checks.form_inference calls Medallion → Exception fee a loop; as drawn it is a back-edge to the itinerary's start, and the closing half is drawn only for Unbilled input and Tax shape. The relabel states the closure analytically; the repairer should say 'a loop stated in one label and drawn in two edges' rather than 'a loop the itinerary conceals'.

Loyalty penalty's 'ended in one market only by a rule that priced newcomers and renewers alike' (the 2022 UK insurance pricing rule) and Tax shape's felt-soled sneaker are documented and correctly asserted; Unit mismatch's beekeeper is humor and reads as such. No other promotion found.
duplication: None against the grown lists: leverage-discoveries' rounding rule was deliberately excluded by the author, ghost-leverages' advertiser case is about power that outlived its source, and exchange-ontologies' Priority is the author's own unresolved seed, not a member. Adjacencies with sibling maps in this fleet, not yet grown: what-a-price-does' 'Quote that cannot be compared' and 'Price that goes to sleep' touch Unit mismatch and Loyalty penalty from the price's side; pricing-unit-metamorphoses' 'Reader becomes the ton' and 'Audit is the unit' share the newspaper and bookseller cases with Second payer and Given-away option. This map adds, in each case, the carrier that holds the margin and the outsider's tell, which those maps do not name; the shared cases should be tolerated, not deduplicated.
best_unresolved_seed: The rented right: Medallion covers a hiding place bought once and paid to whoever held it first, but the airport concession, the prison phone contract's commission to the state, the franchise fee, and the slotting fee are the same found margin paid yearly to whoever holds the door now, so the margin stays visible as the landlord's rent, present tense, neither the operator's nor the past's. It would give the map's loop its documented closing half (Popcorn → rented right: the airport water bottle's margin is in the concession rent) and it asks whether a hiding place that is rented rather than owned ever recruits the next one, since the rent can be raised to take it.
independent_review_line: Fable critic: admitted after repairing six items whose cases contradicted their own carrier or grantor (a warranty read as breakage, a captive phone call and a checked bag read as deviations, a supplier-granted option read as customer-granted, a tip read as an hour priced at zero, an idle lot read as a byproduct), relabeling Medallion → Exception fee to drop an undocumented case and state the loop as analytical, and moving Financing beside Float and Lot to distribution beside Supplier's clock so the seriation note is true of the order.
